clue.text: Drug found at university — put one's foot down

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, a drug
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A drug has turned up on campus and someone is putting their foot down about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' looks like taking a firm stand, but here it means pressing the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting your foot down on the accelerator makes a car go faster, an idiom for accelerating.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is is read from bottom to top

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning or about

explanation.surface: Dad has got out of bed and is moving around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up and about' reads as Dad out of bed; 'up' is the reversal signal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to father a child is to beget it, especially said of a stallion.

clue.text: Creatures having feet with a point at each end

indicators.note: says a compass point stands at either end of the abbreviation for feet, enclosing it

parts.note: E and S are points of the compass, east and south

explanation.surface: Animals with pointed feet at both ends, like some strange beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a point' is used twice: one compass point (E) at the front and another (S) at the back of FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts in their young land stage are a crossword-favourite kind of small amphibian creature.

clue.text: Way to serve potatoes, just stuffed with game

indicators.note: the word for just is filled with the word for the game

parts.note: due means deserved or just, as in 'his just deserts'
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Potatoes served simply, alongside a stuffed game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests pheasant or venison with the potatoes, but it is chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesse potatoes are a classic French preparation of piped, baked mashed potato.

indicators.note: the wrong version of the word plane means its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger boards the wrong aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like the verb for getting on a plane; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a board, such as a group of judges or a flat sheet of wood.

clue.text: Big cuts she makes in fuel

indicators.note: the word she is placed inside the word for fuel

parts.note: gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: A woman making big cuts in fuel spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Gashes are deep wounds, long big cuts in the skin.

clue.text: Throwing out an egg I found no longer fresh

indicators.note: throwing the letters out of order rearranges an egg I

explanation.surface: Someone throws out an egg that has gone stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing out' reads as discarding the egg; it rearranges AN EGG I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something growing old or ageing is past its freshness, getting older.

clue.text: It makes sound sense to those in need

definitions.text: It makes sound sense to those in need

parts.words: It makes sound sense to those in need
parts.note: a device that lets the hard of hearing make sense of sound

explanation.surface: Something that makes perfect sense to people who need it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound sense' reads as good judgement, but it is the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amplifier worn in the ear that helps deaf people perceive sounds.

indicators.note: in a down clue, the second word sits on, below, the first in the reading order

parts.note: to screen a film is to project it
a play is a dramatic work

explanation.surface: Working on a project for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work on' looks like a phrase meaning toil at; 'on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The script of a movie, the written version from which a picture is shot.

indicators.note: one word sits within the period of another, so it goes inside

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break

indicators.note: back means the word for call is read in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness

explanation.surface: During a break, someone calls their mother back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not mother but silent, as in keeping mum; 'back' signals the reversal and 'During' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum means keeping quiet, so a reserved, silent person is taciturn.

parts.note: a broken couple can be paired again, so to fix it is literally to pair once more

explanation.surface: Patching up a failing marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something broken is to mend it, and a couple paired again is a re-pairing.

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a key opens a lock

explanation.surface: A cricket team's opening batsman performed poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like an opening batsman, but it is a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Music played out of tune is badly performed, not at the right pitch.

parts.note: a din from the infernal regions, or a criminal gang's scheme

explanation.surface: A gangland scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld racket' suggests organised crime, but read literally it is a din from the infernal regions.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial phrase for a very loud din, from the place of the damned.

clue.text: Cutting I sign with cross, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of I sign and cross could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone cuts out a form and signs it with a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting with a pair of shears or blades is the action named by the verb.

parts.note: not a bad situation but the state of being sorry, contrition

explanation.surface: Things are in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sorry state' means a mess; read literally it is the condition of being sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrition for wrongdoing is the condition of feeling sorry.

definitions.meaning: slang for photographs of scantily dressed attractive women
a sweet tart made with soft cheese on a biscuit base

explanation.surface: A pin-up of an exposed hussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a slur continuing the pin-up picture, but it is a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a dessert pie with a soft cheese filling and slang for glamour photographs.

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
axed means cut down, as trees or budgets

explanation.surface: A company was persuaded to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade gently, so coaxed means persuaded.

definitions.meaning: a college servant at Cambridge and Durham
to give someone ... is to give them pain

explanation.surface: A college servant who is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a Cambridge college servant and an informal British word for pain or trouble.

definitions.meaning: chips are tokens used in games or gambling
people or machines that count, reckon

explanation.surface: Microchips for computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' and 'computers' look like electronics; one means gaming tokens, the other things that count.
explanation.definitionFit: Both tokens used in games and those that count or reckon things.

definitions.meaning: to take legal action against someone

explanation.surface: A girl decides to take action.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a girl's name and the verb for bringing a lawsuit.

parts.note: the naked rider on horseback watched by Peeping Tom in the Coventry legend

explanation.surface: Tom studies the shape of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend, she rode naked through Coventry and Peeping Tom was the one man who looked.
explanation.definitionFit: The noblewoman of Coventry legend who rode naked on a horse, spied on by Peeping Tom.

clue.text: Famine for a large number on this planet

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letter sits on top of the planet

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
Earth is the planet we live on

explanation.surface: Famine afflicts a great many people on this planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, as of food in a famine.

indicators.note: disrupting the letters of the indolence throws them into a new order

explanation.surface: Failing to shake off laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in decline is failing or getting worse.

indicators.note: the word for fat goes round the numeral for one

parts.note: lard is pig fat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fat, round Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a description of the man, but it puts LARD round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner, a Scotsman of property.

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the words a and delay upside down, reading upward

parts.note: lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A delay spoils the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A LAG over to GAL A.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or celebration.

definitions.meaning: a pole such as a mast or boom on a ship

explanation.surface: A crate made of a ship's wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container; it is the verb for fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the verb for practice boxing and a pole used as a mast or yard on a ship.

indicators.note: a desolate, ruined region has its letters wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: An abandoned area left uncared for.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to neglect it, take no notice of it.

clue.text: Got rid of electric current and got gas

parts.note: fired means dismissed, got rid of
amp, short for ampere, is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Someone sacked the electrician and was left with gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and got' are link words before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane, the explosive gas found in coal mines.

clue.text: The ego trip of a German writer

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of the ego fall about

explanation.surface: A German author on an ego trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ego trip' looks like a phrase; 'trip' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, author of Faust, the great German poet.

indicators.note: a sunk ship is wrecked, so the letters of padre is are thrown about

explanation.surface: A priest is feeling deeply depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is hopelessness, a state of deep gloom.
